title: Nvidia Stock Fell 14% Before Trump Urged Huang's Return
summary: Nvidia stock fell 14% Friday on an SEC probe report. Trump then urged the board to rehire Jensen Huang as Washington seeks answers on China chip sales.
body_markdown:
## Nvidia (NVDA): Shares Fell 23% in Worst Week Since 2008


Nvidia shares fell 23% last week, their worst week since the 2008 financial crisis, leaving the stock nearly 48% below its Oct. 6 record high, according to[Investing.com](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-shares-fall-115-as-report-of-sec-accounting-probe-adds-to-pressure-4973044) . Nvidia, once the world's most valuable company, now ranks fourth behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet, per Seeking Alpha.


[Selling picked up on Friday](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-23-2026/) after Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company, and the shares had already fallen about 7% before that news emerged, Investing.com reported. The SEC declined to comment. An SEC investigation does not establish wrongdoing, the outlet noted.


The slide outweighed a strong[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) on Nov. 17. Nvidia posted third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double a year earlier, with data center revenue up 110% to $107.6 billion. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, per Investing.com.


## Bessent and House Democrats Press Nvidia on China Chip Sales


On CBS's "Face the Nation" on Sunday, Bessent said the U.S. is seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company, as reported by Seeking Alpha. "We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers," Bessent said. "It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was."


House Democrats have opened a separate probe. Representatives Gregory Meeks, ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Nov. 19, asking what influence Nvidia wielded over a Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed for possible illegal diversion of chips to China, according to[Reuters](https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/sci-tech/2026-11-20-probe-into-nvidias-influence-on-us-megaspeed-chips-case/) . The letter asks for answers and documents by Dec. 1.


Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia partner that operates data centers, has been under U.S. investigation for two years, the Commerce and Justice departments said, per Reuters. Investigators interviewed former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy, during a June 2025 inspection; China has denied that she is a spy. Megaspeed says it complies with all applicable laws, and Nvidia said, "We look forward to engaging with Congress on this matter."


## AMD (AMD): Shares Fell About 7% on Short Seller's China Claims


Scrutiny of China ties has also reached Nvidia's rival. Shares of[Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) fell about 7% after Hunterbrook Media, which disclosed a short position in the stock, alleged that blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems kept receiving updated AMD firmware,[International Business Times](https://www.ibtimes.com/amd-shares-fall-hunterbrook-china-export-risks-3809979) reported on Nov. 19. The report came amid investigations into Nvidia's sales to Asian companies with ties to China, and AMD had been viewed as a potential beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia, the outlet said.


Hunterbrook said AMD bills more than 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong. AMD rejected the report. "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," a spokesperson said, adding that "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations." According to IBTimes, the allegations have not established that AMD violated federal export rules, and Hunterbrook could benefit financially from a decline in AMD's valuation.
